nodes.content: Design a tiered MVCC storage engine preserving snapshot isolation and safe reclamation during concurrent migration, writes, and crashes.
requirements: Acknowledged writes and snapshot-required versions survive crashes at every migration and reclamation transition.
Migration increases p99 read latency by at most 20% versus identical workloads without migration.

nodes.content: Use fsync-before-ack MVCC WAL, durable snapshot pins, copy-fsync-then-publish manifests, pin-gated reclamation, and read-priority migration throttling.
Which durable ordering keeps concurrently written, snapshot-pinned versions reachable across manifest publication and extent reclamation?
Persisted snapshot pins and WAL, followed by copy-fsync, WAL-tail replay, manifest-fsync, then reclamation, yield zero missing versions under crash injection.
Specify durable migration invariants, implement WAL-tail replay and pin-gated reclamation, then crash-test every fsync boundary during concurrent writes and snapshots.
Run CrashMatrix-48 across migration fsync and reclamation boundaries with concurrent writes and pinned snapshots, checking recovered version visibility.
CrashMatrix-48 found 1/48 failures: a post-replay acknowledged write vanished when manifest-fsync advanced the WAL checkpoint beyond its unapplied sequence.
Checkpoint only through manifest-applied WAL sequence, retaining later records and persisted pins; CrashMatrix-48 should recover all acknowledged and pinned versions.
Patch checkpointing to the manifest-applied WAL sequence, then rerun CrashMatrix-48 with post-replay writes and pinned snapshots.
Patched CrashMatrix-48 recovered every acknowledged write and pinned version in 48/48 crash-boundary cases, including post-replay writes.
After CrashMatrix-48 passes, benchmark identical 90%-read TierBench-1M workloads with and without read-priority migration; measure p99 read-latency inflation.
TierBench-1M report records p99 read latency of 4.0 ms baseline versus 4.6 ms during migration (+15%).
Adopt pin-gated reclamation, manifest-applied WAL checkpointing, and read-priority migration: CrashMatrix-48 passed 48/48; TierBench-1M p99 increased 15%.
Use a shared durable WAL, immutable shadow SSTables, generation-CAS routing, durable snapshot watermarks, and foreground-reserved migration credits.
Using TierBench-1M’s 4.0 ms baseline, implement generation-CAS shadow routing, watermark reclamation, and migration credits; verify crash safety and p99≤4.8 ms.
Implement generation-CAS shadow routing and durable snapshot watermarks; run ShadowCrash-64 across WAL, routing, and reclamation boundaries.
ShadowCrash-64 report records 64/64 crash-boundary recoveries of acknowledged and snapshot-required versions using generation-CAS routing and durable watermarks.
Given ShadowCrash-64’s 64/64 recoveries, can foreground-reserved migration credits keep TierBench-1M p99 read latency ≤4.8 ms?
Rerun ShadowCrash-64 and TierBench-1M with foreground-reserved credits; verify 64/64 recoveries and compare p99 against the 4.0 ms baseline.
ShadowCrash-64 retained 64/64 recoveries; TierBench-1M migration p99 reached 4.5 ms versus 4.0 ms baseline (+12.5%).
Adopt p2’s shadow-routing design instead of n11’s: ShadowCrash-64 passed 64/64; TierBench-1M migration p99 fell from 4.6 to 4.5 ms.
After ShadowCrash-64, run PinChurn-72 on both designs with six-hour snapshots and overwrites, checking crash recovery and migration p99.
PinChurn-72: baseline p99 5.0 ms; p1 reached 6.3 ms (+26%), p2 5.7 ms (+14%); both recovered 72/72 crashes.
Durable WAL, generation-CAS routing, and snapshot watermarks preserve required versions; reserved credits limit migration p99 inflation below 20%.
Run WatermarkChaos-96 across snapshot release, CAS publication, concurrent writes, and crashes; verify required-version recovery and migration p99≤1.2× baseline.
WatermarkChaos-96: 1/96 crashes lost a pinned version when reclamation followed an unfsynced snapshot release; migration p99 stayed within 20%.
Extend p2 with WAL-fsynced snapshot-release tombstones and epoch-fenced reclamation; delete old SSTables only after durable release and reader quiescence.
When can old SSTables be reclaimed after snapshot release without losing crash-recovered pins or disrupting in-flight readers?
Reclaim only after release-tombstone fsync, surviving-pin watermark recalculation, and reader-epoch quiescence; WatermarkChaos-96 should recover 96/96 versions.
Implement tombstone-fsync and epoch-fenced reclamation; rerun WatermarkChaos-96 for 96/96 recoveries and p99≤4.8 ms against TierBench-1M’s 4.0 ms baseline.
Patched WatermarkChaos-96 recovered required versions in 96/96 crashes; TierBench-1M migration p99 was 4.6 ms versus 4.0 ms baseline (+15%).
Replace p2’s unsafe release reclamation with p3’s fsynced tombstones and epoch fencing; patched crashes pass 96/96, migration p99 +15%.
Zero per-SSTable reader counts permit safe deletion after durable release and watermark recalculation, reducing reclaim lag versus global epoch fencing.
Prototype per-SSTable reader counts, compare reclaim lag with epoch fencing, and inject crashes around durable release and file deletion.
After adopting epoch fencing, run ReclaimRace-128 comparing per-SSTable counts against epochs for crash-safe deletion and p99 reclaim lag.
ReclaimRace-128: both variants recovered 128/128 crashes; per-SSTable counts reduced p99 reclaim lag from 180 ms (epochs) to 45 ms.
After ReclaimRace-128, stress zero-count deletion against concurrent route lookup and reader-count acquisition; check use-after-free and snapshot visibility.
RouteRace-256 found 1/256 failures: deletion observed zero readers before route lookup acquired its count, breaking an active snapshot read.
Can atomic route-pin acquisition prevent RouteRace-256’s deletion race while retaining ReclaimRace-128’s 45 ms p99 reclaim lag?
Lock-coupled route lookup and reader-count acquisition, then unpublish-and-drain deletion, prevent RouteRace-256 failures while retaining 45 ms p99 reclaim lag.
Implement lock-coupled route pins and unpublish-and-drain deletion; rerun RouteRace-256 and ReclaimRace-128, measuring failures and p99 reclaim lag.
Patched RouteRace-256 passed 256/256; ReclaimRace-128 recovered 128/128 crashes with 45 ms p99 reclaim lag versus epochs’ 180 ms.
Adopt tombstone-gated, lock-coupled per-SSTable pins: RouteRace-256 passed 256/256, ReclaimRace-128 recovered 128/128, and p99 reclaim lag remained 45 ms.
Build fsynced shared-WAL MVCC with generation-CAS shadow routing, durable snapshot pins and release tombstones, lock-coupled reclamation, and foreground-reserved migration credits.
Integrate n39’s lock-coupled pins into p4; run IntegratedChaos-192 for crash-safe snapshot isolation and TierBench-1M for migration p99≤1.2× baseline.
After ShadowCrash-64, run IntegratedChaos-192 on p4’s lock-coupled routing, then TierBench-1M; verify version recovery and migration p99≤4.8 ms.
IntegratedChaos-192 recovered acknowledged and pinned versions in 192/192 crashes; TierBench-1M migration p99 was 4.7 ms versus 4.0 ms (+17.5%).
After IntegratedChaos-192, run SoakMix-24h with disk saturation, snapshot churn, migration, and crashes; verify recovered versions and p99≤1.2× baseline.
SoakMix-24h report: 24/24 crashes preserved acknowledged and pinned versions; migration read p99 was 5.9 ms versus 5.0 ms baseline (+18%).
Adopt p4: IntegratedChaos-192 and SoakMix-24h preserved versions in 192/192 and 24/24 crashes; migration p99 inflation stayed ≤18%.
Replace shadow-SSTable copying with WAL-backed per-range handoffs and immutable delta overlays; reclaim pinned extents only after durable checkpoints.
Can WAL-backed range handoffs reduce SoakMix-24h’s 18% migration p99 inflation without compromising its 24/24 crash recoveries?
WAL-backed range handoffs with immutable delta overlays keep SoakMix-24h crash recovery at 24/24 while reducing migration p99 inflation below 18%.
Prototype p5 range handoffs; rerun SoakMix-24h with matched load, comparing crash recoveries and migration p99 against p4’s 24/24 and +18%.
SoakMix-24h with p5 recovered versions in 24/24 crashes; migration read p99 was 5.5 ms versus 5.0 ms baseline (+10%).
Given p5’s +10% and p4’s adoption, specify handoff checkpoint invariants, expand crash testing, and retain p4 unless snapshot safety holds.
Using SoakMix-24h’s recovery baseline, run HandoffCrash-256 across checkpoint fsync, pinned-extent retirement, concurrent overwrites, and crash recovery.
HandoffCrash-256 report: 255/256 recoveries; one crash after checkpoint fsync lost a pinned pre-handoff version during extent retirement.
Defer p5 despite +10% p99 inflation: HandoffCrash-256 lost a pinned version; retain adopted p4’s lock-coupled, tombstone-gated reclamation.
